strokeOrderNote: one stroke — the manual numbers four movements; native writers draw them without lifting, and this ductus follows them in order, coming back along the middle bar to the crossing before it turns around the lower-left bowl; cited to Radhakrishnan, Tamil Script Learners Manual, Frame 3, ச

strokeOrderSource.citation: Sankaran Radhakrishnan, Tamil Script Learners Manual, Appendix I: Hand-movements, Frame 3, ச (University of Texas at Austin), p. 191
strokeOrderSource.variation: Frame 3 numbers three upper-frame movements and a fourth that turns around ச's lower-left bowl. Native writers draw the four movements as one continuous stroke, and this ductus follows them in order without lifting: movement 3 ends at the tip of the middle bar, so the pen comes back along the bar to the inner crossing before it turns around the bowl. In HP Labs India's online Tamil handwriting data (the LipiTk 4.0 Tamil isolated-character recognizer, trained on hpl-tamil-iso-char), 88% of the 176 stored prototypes of ச are a single pen-down stroke. Tamil handwriting varies by school; this is one attested order fitted to the bundled Noto Sans Tamil outline.

notes: Ca is the simpler sibling of க: both begin with the same upper frame, but ச keeps only the rounded lower-left bowl and lets the middle bar project to the right. The final movement closes that bowl back at the crossing. Its four numbered movements are one continuous stroke: the upper frame, the projecting middle bar, and the lower-left bowl follow one another without a lift.
